detailed_description: Image Splitter Online divides one uploaded image into a simple rows-and-columns grid directly in the browser. Use presets such as 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, 2x3, and 3x2, or enter custom row and column counts from 1 to 10. The page shows the original size, the calculated part size, and a grid overlay before splitting. When you click Split, Canvas creates equal rectangular PNG pieces from the selected grid. You can download a single piece from the preview or download all generated PNG files together as a ZIP archive. The tool is designed for social grid drafts, classroom image pieces, layout mockups, and quick visual review; it does not add overlap, choose output formats, preserve metadata, or create sprite-sheet workflows.
usage_steps: Upload one image from the file picker.
Choose a grid preset such as 3x3, or set rows and columns manually from 1 to 10.
Review the red grid overlay, original size, and calculated part size.
Click Split to generate equal PNG pieces in the browser with Canvas.
Download one piece from the preview or use Download All to save every PNG in a ZIP file.
usage_examples: Split a poster draft into a 3x3 grid for a social media layout preview.
Create equal PNG pieces from a large illustration for classroom or puzzle activities.
Break a banner into a 2x3 grid so a designer can review each section separately.
Export all generated parts as a ZIP after checking the grid overlay and part size.

faqs.question: What does Image Splitter Online create?
faqs.answer: It creates equal rectangular PNG pieces from one uploaded image based on the selected row and column grid.

faqs.question: Can I set custom rows and columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can use presets such as 2x2 and 3x3, or enter row and column values from 1 to 10.

faqs.question: Can I download all pieces at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use Download All after splitting to save every PNG piece in a ZIP file.

faqs.question: Does the tool process images on a server?
faqs.answer: No. Upload, preview, splitting, single-piece download, and ZIP creation happen in the browser.

faqs.question: Does it support overlap, EXIF preservation, or output format selection?
faqs.answer: No. The current tool focuses on simple non-overlapping PNG grid pieces created from rows and columns.
